450:     async fn consume(
451:         &self,
452:         command: ConsumeLoginLink,
453:     ) -> Result<ConsumedLoginLink, ConsumeLoginLinkError> {
454:         let now = (self.clock)();
455:         let Some(token) = SecretToken::parse(command.token) else {
456:             audit_consume_failure(&self.pool, None, "malformed_token", now).await?;
457:             return Err(ConsumeLoginLinkError::Invalid);
458:         };
459:         let token_hash = self.secret_key.hash_token(TokenDomain::Login, &token);
460:         let mut transaction = self.pool.begin_with("BEGIN IMMEDIATE").await?;
461:         let record = sqlx::query_as::<_, LoginTokenUser>(
462:             "SELECT login_tokens.id AS token_id, login_tokens.expires_at,
463:                     login_tokens.revoked_at, login_tokens.consumed_at,
464:                     users.id AS user_id, users.normalized_email, users.display_name,
465:                     users.status, users.is_superadmin
466:              FROM login_tokens
467:              JOIN users ON users.id = login_tokens.user_id
468:              WHERE login_tokens.token_hash = ?",
469:         )
470:         .bind(token_hash.as_bytes().as_slice())
471:         .fetch_optional(&mut *transaction)
472:         .await?;
473: 
474:         let Some(record) = record else {
475:             audit_consume_failure_in_transaction(&mut transaction, None, "token_not_found", now)
476:                 .await?;
477:             transaction.commit().await?;
478:             return Err(ConsumeLoginLinkError::Invalid);
479:         };
480:         if let Some(reason) = record.rejection_reason(now) {
481:             audit_consume_failure_in_transaction(
482:                 &mut transaction,
483:                 Some(record.token_id),
484:                 reason,
485:                 now,
486:             )
487:             .await?;
488:             transaction.commit().await?;
489:             return Err(ConsumeLoginLinkError::Invalid);
490:         }
491: 
492:         sqlx::query(
493:             "UPDATE login_tokens SET consumed_at = ?
494:              WHERE id = ? AND consumed_at IS NULL",
495:         )
496:         .bind(now)
497:         .bind(record.token_id)
498:         .execute(&mut *transaction)
499:         .await?;
500: 
501:         if let Some(prior_session) = command.prior_session_token.and_then(SecretToken::parse) {
502:             let prior_hash = self
503:                 .secret_key
504:                 .hash_token(TokenDomain::Session, &prior_session);
505:             sqlx::query(
506:                 "UPDATE sessions SET revoked_at = ?
507:                  WHERE session_hash = ? AND revoked_at IS NULL",
508:             )
509:             .bind(now)
510:             .bind(prior_hash.as_bytes().as_slice())
511:             .execute(&mut *transaction)
512:             .await?;
513:         }
514: 
515:         let session_token = self.secret_key.generate_token();
516:         let session_hash = self
517:             .secret_key
518:             .hash_token(TokenDomain::Session, &session_token);
519:         sqlx::query(
520:             "INSERT INTO sessions (
521:                 user_id, session_hash, expires_at, revoked_at, created_at, last_seen_at
522:              ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, NULL, ?, ?)",
523:         )
524:         .bind(record.user_id)
525:         .bind(session_hash.as_bytes().as_slice())
526:         .bind(now + self.session_lifetime_seconds)
527:         .bind(now)
528:         .bind(now)
529:         .execute(&mut *transaction)
530:         .await?;
531:         sqlx::query("UPDATE users SET last_login_at = ? WHERE id = ?")
532:             .bind(now)
533:             .bind(record.user_id)
534:             .execute(&mut *transaction)
535:             .await?;
536:         insert_audit_in_transaction(
537:             &mut transaction,
538:             Some(record.user_id),
539:             CONSUME_SUCCEEDED_ACTION,
540:             "login_token",
541:             Some(record.token_id.to_string()),
542:             r#"{"result":"authenticated"}"#,
543:             now,
544:         )
545:         .await?;
546:         transaction.commit().await?;
547: 
548:         let csrf_token = self.secret_key.generate_csrf_token(&session_token);
549:         tracing::info!("login link consumed");
550:         Ok(ConsumedLoginLink {
551:             user: ActiveUser {
552:                 id: record.user_id,
553:                 email: record.normalized_email,
554:                 display_name: record.display_name,
555:                 status: "registered",
556:                 is_superadmin: record.is_superadmin,
557:             },
558:             session_token,
559:             csrf_token,
560:         })
561:     }

584:             ),

597:             }
598:         };
599: 
600:         let session_token = self.secret_key.generate_token();

609:         .bind(user_id)
610:         .bind(session_hash.as_bytes().as_slice())
611:         .bind(now + self.session_lifetime_seconds)
612:         .bind(now)
613:         .bind(now)
614:         .execute(&mut *transaction)
615:         .await
616:         .map_err(|e| DevLoginError::Database(e.to_string()))?;
617: 
618:         let csrf_token = self.secret_key.generate_csrf_token(&session_token);
619:         let redirect_url = format!("/dev-login?csrf_token={}", csrf_token.expose());
620:         let cookie = SessionCookieBuilder::new(&session_token)
621:             .is_secure(self.is_secure)
622:             .build();
623: 
624:         transaction
625:             .commit()
626:             .await
627:             .map_err(|e| DevLoginError::Database(e.to_string()))?;
628: 
629:         Ok(DevLoginResult {
630:             redirect_url,
631:             cookie,
632:         })
633:     }

746: impl LoginTokenUser {
747:     fn rejection_reason(&self, now: i64) -> Option<&'static str> {
748:         if self.status != "registered" {
749:             Some("account_ineligible")
750:         } else if self.revoked_at.is_some() {
751:             Some("revoked")
752:         } else if self.consumed_at.is_some() {
753:             Some("already_consumed")
754:         } else if now >= self.expires_at {
755:             Some("expired")
756:         } else {
757:             None
758:         }
759:     }
760: }

770: fn build_application_router(state: ApplicationState) -> Router {
771:     let mut router = Router::new()
772:         .route("/health/live", get(health_live))
773:         .route("/health/ready", get(health_ready))
774:         .route("/api/v1/auth/invitations/consume", post(consume_invitation))
775:         .route("/api/v1/auth/invitations/preview", get(preview_invitation))
776:         .route("/api/v1/auth/login-links", post(request_login_link))
777:         .route("/api/v1/auth/login-links/consume", post(consume_login_link))
778:         .fallback(not_found);
779:     if state.password_login_enabled {
780:         router = router.route("/api/v1/auth/password-login", post(password_login));
781:     }
782:     if std::env::var("APP_ENV").ok().as_deref() == Some("development") {
783:         router = router.route("/api/v1/dev/login", get(dev_login));
784:     }
785:     if state.shared_view_service.is_some() && state.event_service.is_some() {
786:         let mut public = Router::new()
787:             .route("/api/v1/public/views/:token", get(read_public_view))
788:             .route(
789:                 "/api/v1/public/views/:token/events",
790:                 get(list_public_view_events),
791:             )
792:             .route("/api/v1/public/views/:token/feed.ics", get(feed_ics))
793:             .layer(middleware::from_fn(public_response_headers));
794:         if let Some(limiter) = state.public_rate_limiter.clone() {
795:             public = public.layer(middleware::from_fn_with_state(
796:                 limiter,
797:                 crate::public_rate_limit::public_rate_limit_middleware,
798:             ));
799:         }
800:         router = router.merge(public);
801:     }
802:     if let Some(manager) = state.session_manager.clone() {
803:         let mut protected = Router::new()

983: fn redact_sensitive_path(uri: &axum::http::Uri) -> String {
984:     let path = uri.path();
985:     let safe_path = if path.starts_with("/api/v1/public/views/") {
986:         "/api/v1/public/views/[REDACTED]"
987:     } else {
988:         path
989:     };
990: 
991:     let query = uri.query().unwrap_or("");
992:     if query.is_empty() {
993:         return safe_path.to_owned();
994:     }
995: 
996:     let mut has_redaction = false;
997:     let redacted_pairs: Vec<String> = query
998:         .split('&')
999:         .map(|pair| {
1000:             if let Some((key, _)) = pair.split_once('=')
1001:                 && SENSITIVE_QUERY_KEYS.contains(&key)
1002:             {
1003:                 has_redaction = true;
1004:                 return format!("{key}=[REDACTED]");
1005:             }
1006:             pair.to_owned()
1007:         })
1008:         .collect();
1009: 
1010:     if has_redaction {
1011:         format!("{}?{}", safe_path, redacted_pairs.join("&"))
1012:     } else {
1013:         safe_path.to_owned()
1014:     }
1015: }
1016: 
1017: const SENSITIVE_QUERY_KEYS: &[&str] = &[
1018:     "token",
1019:     "csrf_token",
1020:     "api_key",
1021:     "Authorization",
1022:     "session",
1023:     "refresh_token",
1024: ];

2: //
3: // Returns the user's calendars filtered by McpGrant permissions.

25: /// Handle the calendar_list tool call.
26: ///
27: /// Authorization pipeline:
28: /// 1. Auth middleware validates the OAuth token and publishes the identity.
29: /// 2. Service layer resolves the authoritative grant.
30: /// 3. Check the grant's calendar-list permission.
31: /// 4. Call CommonCal core to list calendars.
32: /// 5. Filter by the grant's allowed_calendar_ids.
33: /// 6. Return the structured response.
34: pub async fn handle(
35:     context: &AuthorizedToolContext<'_>,
36:     _params: CalendarListParams,
37: ) -> Result<Response<axum::body::Body>, ToolError> {
38:     let grant = context.grant;
39: 
40:     // Check tool permission against the authoritative grant.
41:     //
42:     // calendar_list is a calendar-metadata read; it is gated by the
43:     // availability/metadata capability, NOT by the availability_find tool
44:     // capability. (Previously this checked the wrong capability.)
45:     if !crate::mcp_grant::check_tool_permission(grant, "calendar_list") {
46:         return Err(ToolError::Forbidden(
47:             "calendar_list requires calendar metadata read permission".to_string(),
48:         ));
49:     }
50: 
51:     // Fetch calendars from CommonCal core.
52:     let calendars = context
53:         .internal_client
54:         .list_calendars(context.token.user_id)
55:         .await
56:         .map_err(|e| ToolError::Internal(format!("calendar fetch failed: {}", e)))?;
57: 
58:     // Filter by the grant's allowed calendars.
59:     let filtered: Vec<CalendarSummary> = calendars
60:         .into_iter()
61:         .filter(|c| check_calendar_access(grant, c.id))
62:         .map(|c| CalendarSummary {
63:             id: c.id,
64:             name: c.name,
65:             color: String::new(),
66:             access: c.access,
67:         })
68:         .collect();
69: 
70:     // Build structured response.
71:     let output = ToolOutput {
72:         content: vec![ContentBlock::Text {

74:                 calendars: filtered,
75:             })
76:             .unwrap_or_else(|_| "[]".to_string()),
77:         }],

83:     Ok(Response::builder()
84:         .status(StatusCode::OK)
85:         .header("content-type", "application/json")

146:     /// Audience: the internal service name
147:     pub async fn exchange_token(
148:         &self,
149:         subject_token: &str,
150:         actor_token: Option<&str>,
151:         resource: &str,
152:     ) -> Result<TokenExchangeResponse, InternalError> {
153:         let url = self
154:             .api_base
155:             .join("internal/token-exchange")
156:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Connection(format!("failed to join URL: {}", e)))?;
157: 
158:         let mut body = serde_json::json!({
159:             "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange",
160:             "subject_token": subject_token,
161:             "subject_token_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token",
162:             "audience": "commoncal-internal",
163:             "resource": [resource],
164:         });
165: 
166:         if let Some(actor) = actor_token {
167:             body["actor_token"] = serde_json::json!(actor);
168:             body["actor_token_type"] =
169:                 serde_json::json!("urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token");
170:         }
171: 
172:         let resp = self
173:             .http_client
174:             .post(url.as_str())
175:             .header("x-mcp-api-key", &self.api_key)
176:             .json(&body)
177:             .send()
178:             .await
179:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Connection(e.to_string()))?;
180: 
181:         if !resp.status().is_success() {
182:             let status = resp.status().as_u16();
183:             let body_text = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_else(|_| "no body".to_string());
184:             tracing::warn!(
185:                 status,
186:                 body = %body_text,
187:                 "token exchange failed"
188:             );
189:             return Err(InternalError::Http(
190:                 status,
191:                 "token exchange failed".to_string(),
192:             ));
193:         }
194: 
195:         let exchange_resp: TokenExchangeResponse = resp
196:             .json()
197:             .await
198:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Deserialize(e.to_string()))?;
199: 
200:         Ok(exchange_resp)
201:     }

548:     /// Resolve the single authoritative MCP grant for a user + OAuth client.
549:     ///
550:     /// CommonCal core is the source of truth for grants. The internal endpoint
551:     /// returns a vector; a well-formed response contains exactly one grant.
552:     /// Zero grants is a normal authorization outcome (`Ok(None)`); more than one
553:     /// is ambiguous core data and fails closed rather than selecting arbitrarily.
554:     pub async fn get_mcp_grant(
555:         &self,
556:         user_id: i64,
557:         client_id: &str,
558:     ) -> Result<Option<McpGrantResponse>, InternalError> {
559:         let mut url = self
560:             .api_base
561:             .join("internal/mcp/mcp-grants")
562:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Connection(format!("failed to join URL: {}", e)))?;
563:         url.query_pairs_mut()
564:             .append_pair("user_id", &user_id.to_string())
565:             .append_pair("client_id", client_id);
566:         let resp = self
567:             .http_client
568:             .get(url.as_str())
569:             .header("x-mcp-api-key", &self.api_key)
570:             .send()
571:             .await
572:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Connection(e.to_string()))?;
573: 
574:         if !resp.status().is_success() {
575:             return Err(InternalError::Http(
576:                 resp.status().as_u16(),
577:                 "get_mcp_grant failed".to_string(),
578:             ));
579:         }
580: 
581:         let grants = resp
582:             .json::<Vec<McpGrantResponse>>()
583:             .await
584:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Deserialize(e.to_string()))?;
585: 
586:         match grants.len() {
587:             0 => Ok(None),
588:             1 => Ok(Some(grants.into_iter().next().unwrap())),
589:             _ => Err(InternalError::Http(
590:                 500,
591:                 "ambiguous grant response: expected at most one grant".to_string(),
592:             )),
593:         }
594:     }

674:             Self::Http(code, msg) => write!(f, "http {}: {}", code, msg),
675:             Self::Deserialize(msg) => write!(f, "deserialize error: {}", msg),
676:         }

1: // Request/session-safe validated identity context.
2: //
3: // The validated identity is stored in a `tokio` task-local so that each
4: // in-flight request carries its own identity. This is concurrency-safe: two
5: // concurrent clients are processed in distinct tasks, so neither can observe
6: // the other's identity. This deliberately replaces the lab's global
7: // `CURRENT_CLAIMS` slot, which is only safe for sequential traffic.
8: //
9: // The auth middleware sets the value for the duration of the downstream
10: // request; the rmcp tool handlers read it at call time.
11: 
12: use crate::oauth::AuthStrength;
13: 
14: /// The validated identity for the current request.
15: #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
16: pub struct Identity {
17:     pub user_id: i64,
18:     pub client_id: String,
19:     pub scopes: Vec<String>,
20:     pub auth_strength: AuthStrength,
21:     pub auth_time: i64,
22:     pub token_id: String,
23: }
24: 
25: impl Identity {
26:     pub fn has_scope(&self, scope: &str) -> bool {
27:         self.scopes.iter().any(|s| s == scope)
28:     }
29: }
30: 
31: impl From<&crate::oauth::TokenValidationResult> for Identity {
32:     fn from(token: &crate::oauth::TokenValidationResult) -> Self {

38:             auth_time: token.auth_time,
39:             token_id: token.token_id.clone(),
40:         }
41:     }
42: }
43: 
44: tokio::task_local! {
45:     /// The validated identity for the current request, if authenticated.
46:     pub static IDENTITY: Option<Identity>;

52: /// request did not pass the auth middleware). Tool handlers treat `None` as an
53: /// authorization failure and fail closed.

1: // OAuth token validation module.
2: //
3: // Validates access tokens from MCP clients:
4: // - Discovery: fetch `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414) or
5: //   `/.well-known/openid-configuration` (OIDC), verify the returned `issuer`
6: //   exactly matches configuration, then follow its HTTPS `jwks_uri`.
7: // - JWT signature verification via JWKS (bounded TTL cache, one refresh on
8: //   unknown kid for key rotation overlap).
9: // - Standard claims: numeric `sub` (CommonCal user id), `client_id`,
10: //   space-delimited `scope`, `iss`, `aud`, `exp`, `iat`, `jti`.
11: // - Validation: signature, allowed algorithm, kid, exact iss, exact MCP
12: //   audience, exp, iat with small clock skew.
13: //
14: // DPoP validation is handled separately in the security module.

51: /// - `iss`: the issuer URL

53: /// - `exp`: expiry (Unix seconds)

155: /// Stateful token validator with bounded metadata/JWKS caching.
156: ///
157: /// The caches are shared across requests via `Arc<Mutex<...>>`. The TTL
158: /// ensures stale keys are never accepted indefinitely: after the TTL expires,
159: /// the next validation fetches fresh JWKS. If a key is no longer present,
160: /// tokens signed with it are rejected.
161: ///
162: /// Key rotation overlap: when a new key is added to the JWKS, both old and
163: /// new keys are present during the overlap window. The validator accepts
164: /// tokens signed by any key in the current JWKS. If a token's `kid` is not
165: /// found in the cached JWKS, the validator performs one refresh to pick up
166: /// the new key. If the kid is still absent after the refresh, the token is
167: /// rejected.
168: #[derive(Clone)]
169: pub struct TokenValidator {
170:     http_client: reqwest::Client,
171:     metadata_cache: Arc<Mutex<Option<CachedMetadata>>>,
172:     jwks_cache: Arc<Mutex<Option<CachedJwks>>>,
173: }
174: 
175: impl TokenValidator {
176:     pub fn new() -> Self {
177:         Self {
178:             http_client: reqwest::Client::builder()
179:                 .danger_accept_invalid_certs(false)
180:                 .danger_accept_invalid_hostnames(false)
181:                 .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10))
182:                 .build()
183:                 .expect("http client"),
184:             metadata_cache: Arc::new(Mutex::new(None)),
185:             jwks_cache: Arc::new(Mutex::new(None)),
186:         }
187:     }
188: 
189:     /// Validate an MCP access token.
190:     ///
191:     /// Performs:
192:     /// 1. Discover `jwks_uri` from authorization-server metadata (cached).
193:     /// 2. Verify the metadata `issuer` exactly matches the configured issuer.
194:     /// 3. Fetch JWKS from the discovered `jwks_uri` (cached).
195:     /// 4. Parse JWT header to find `kid` and `alg`.
196:     /// 5. Find the matching key by `kid` (one refresh on unknown kid).
197:     /// 6. Verify JWT signature, issuer, audience, exp, iat.
198:     /// 7. Extract standard claims (numeric sub, client_id, scope).
199:     pub async fn validate(
200:         &self,
201:         token: &str,
202:         issuer: &str,
203:         resource: &str,
204:     ) -> Result<TokenValidationResult, TokenError> {
205:         if token.is_empty() {
206:             return Err(TokenError::MissingToken);
207:         }
208: 
209:         // Step 1: Discover jwks_uri (cached).
210:         let jwks_uri = self.discover_jwks_uri(issuer).await?;
211: 
212:         // Step 2: Fetch JWKS (cached).
213:         let mut jwks = self.fetch_jwks(&jwks_uri).await?;
214: 
215:         // Step 3: Parse JWT header.
216:         let header = parse_jwt_header(token)?;
217: 
218:         // Step 4: Find the matching key by kid.
219:         let jwk = match find_jwk(&jwks.keys, &header.kid) {
220:             Some(jwk) => jwk,
221:             None => {
222:                 // One refresh on unknown kid (key rotation overlap).
223:                 tracing::debug!(
224:                     kid = ?header.kid,
225:                     "unknown kid in cached JWKS, refreshing once"
226:                 );
227:                 jwks = self.refresh_jwks(&jwks_uri).await?;
228:                 find_jwk(&jwks.keys, &header.kid).ok_or_else(|| {
229:                     TokenError::InvalidToken(format!(
230:                         "no matching key for kid: {:?}",
231:                         header.kid
232:                     ))
233:                 })?
234:             }
235:         };
236: 
237:         // Step 5: Convert JWK to DecodingKey.
238:         let decoding_key = jwk_to_decoding_key(jwk)?;
239: 
240:         // Step 6: Build validation rules.
241:         let alg = alg_from_jwk(jwk)?;
242:         let mut validation = Validation::new(alg);
243:         validation.set_issuer(&[issuer]);
244:         validation.set_audience(&[resource]);
245:         validation.set_required_spec_claims(&["exp", "iss", "aud", "sub", "iat"]);
246:         validation.leeway = CLOCK_SKEW_SECS;
247: 
248:         // Step 7: Decode and validate the token.
249:         let token_data = decode::<TokenClaims>(token, &decoding_key, &validation)
250:             .map_err(|e| match e.kind() {
251:                 JwtErrorKind::ExpiredSignature => TokenError::Expired,
252:                 JwtErrorKind::InvalidIssuer => TokenError::InvalidIssuer,
253:                 JwtErrorKind::InvalidAudience => TokenError::InvalidAudience,
254:                 JwtErrorKind::InvalidSignature => TokenError::InvalidToken(e.to_string()),
255:                 _ => TokenError::InvalidToken(e.to_string()),
256:             })?;
257: 
258:         // Step 8: Validate iat (not in the future beyond clock skew).
259:         let now = current_time_secs();
260:         if token_data.claims.iat > now + CLOCK_SKEW_SECS as i64 {
261:             return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(
262:                 "iat is in the future beyond clock skew".to_string(),
263:             ));
264:         }
265: 
266:         // Step 9: Extract standard claims.
267:         let claims = &token_data.claims;
268: 
269:         // Parse numeric sub as CommonCal user id.
270:         let user_id: i64 = claims
271:             .sub
272:             .parse()
273:             .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("sub must be a numeric user id".to_string()))?;
274: 
275:         let client_id = claims
276:             .client_id
277:             .clone()
278:             .ok_or_else(|| TokenError::InvalidToken("missing client_id claim".to_string()))?;
279: 
280:         let token_id = claims
281:             .jti
282:             .clone()
283:             .unwrap_or_else(|| uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string());
284: 
285:         // Parse space-delimited scope claim.
286:         let scopes: Vec<String> = claims
287:             .scope
288:             .as_deref()
289:             .map(|s| s.split_whitespace().map(String::from).collect())
290:             .unwrap_or_default();
291: 
292:         // Derive auth strength from amr array.
293:         let auth_strength = derive_auth_strength(claims.amr.as_deref());
294: 
295:         // auth_time from auth_time claim or iat.
296:         let auth_time = claims.auth_time.unwrap_or(claims.iat);
297: 
298:         Ok(TokenValidationResult {
299:             user_id,
300:             oauth_client_id: client_id,
301:             scopes,
302:             auth_strength,
303:             auth_time,
304:             token_id,
305:             expires_at: claims.exp,
306:         })
307:     }
308: 
309:     /// Discover the `jwks_uri` from authorization-server metadata.
310:     ///
311:     /// Tries `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414) first, then
312:     /// falls back to `/.well-known/openid-configuration` (OIDC). Verifies the
313:     /// returned `issuer` exactly matches the configured issuer.
314:     async fn discover_jwks_uri(&self, issuer: &str) -> Result<String, TokenError> {
315:         // Check cache first.
316:         {
317:             let cache = self.metadata_cache.lock().await;
318:             if let Some(entry) = cache.as_ref()
319:                 && entry.fetched_at.elapsed().as_secs() < METADATA_CACHE_TTL_SECS
320:             {
321:                 return Ok(entry.jwks_uri.clone());
322:             }
323:         }
324: 
325:         // Try RFC 8414 location first, then OIDC fallback.
326:         let rfc8414_url = format!("{}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server", issuer.trim_end_matches('/'));
327:         let oidc_url = format!("{}/.well-known/openid-configuration", issuer.trim_end_matches('/'));
328: 
329:         let metadata = match self.fetch_metadata(&rfc8414_url).await {
330:             Ok(m) => m,
331:             Err(_) => self
332:                 .fetch_metadata(&oidc_url)
333:                 .await
334:                 .map_err(|e| TokenError::InvalidToken(format!("discovery failed: {e}")))?,
335:         };
336: 
337:         // Verify issuer matches configuration exactly.
338:         let returned_issuer = metadata
339:             .get("issuer")
340:             .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
341:             .ok_or_else(|| TokenError::InvalidToken("metadata missing issuer".to_string()))?;
342:         if returned_issuer != issuer {
343:             return Err(TokenError::InvalidIssuer);
344:         }
345: 
346:         let jwks_uri = metadata
347:             .get("jwks_uri")
348:             .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
349:             .ok_or_else(|| TokenError::InvalidToken("metadata missing jwks_uri".to_string()))?
350:             .to_string();
351: 
352:         // Validate jwks_uri is a valid absolute URL. Require HTTPS when the
353:         // issuer is HTTPS (production); allow HTTP for loopback test issuers.
354:         let url = url::Url::parse(&jwks_uri)
355:             .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid jwks_uri".to_string()))?;
356:         let issuer_url = url::Url::parse(issuer)
357:             .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid issuer URL".to_string()))?;
358:         if issuer_url.scheme() == "https" && url.scheme() != "https" {
359:             return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(
360:                 "jwks_uri must use https scheme when issuer is https".to_string(),
361:             ));
362:         }
363: 
364:         // Cache the result.
365:         *self.metadata_cache.lock().await = Some(CachedMetadata {
366:             jwks_uri: jwks_uri.clone(),
367:             fetched_at: Instant::now(),
368:         });
369: 
370:         Ok(jwks_uri)
371:     }

373:     /// Fetch authorization-server metadata.
374:     async fn fetch_metadata(&self, url: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
375:         let resp = self
376:             .http_client
377:             .get(url)
378:             .send()
379:             .await
380:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
381: 
382:         if !resp.status().is_success() {
383:             return Err(format!("metadata fetch returned status {}", resp.status()));
384:         }
385: 
386:         let body: serde_json::Value = resp.json().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
387:         Ok(body)
388:     }
389: 
390:     /// Fetch JWKS from the given URI (using cache if fresh).
391:     async fn fetch_jwks(&self, jwks_uri: &str) -> Result<JwksDocument, TokenError> {
392:         // Check cache first.
393:         {
394:             let cache = self.jwks_cache.lock().await;
395:             if let Some(entry) = cache.as_ref()
396:                 && entry.fetched_at.elapsed().as_secs() < JWKS_CACHE_TTL_SECS
397:             {
398:                 return Ok(JwksDocument {
399:                     keys: entry.keys.clone(),
400:                 });
401:             }
402:         }
403: 
404:         self.refresh_jwks(jwks_uri).await
405:     }
406: 
407:     /// Force-refresh JWKS from the given URI (bypasses cache).
408:     async fn refresh_jwks(&self, jwks_uri: &str) -> Result<JwksDocument, TokenError> {
409:         let resp = self
410:             .http_client
411:             .get(jwks_uri)
412:             .send()
413:             .await
414:             .map_err(|e| TokenError::InvalidToken(format!("failed to fetch JWKS: {e}")))?;
415: 
416:         if !resp.status().is_success() {
417:             return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(format!(
418:                 "JWKS fetch returned status {}",
419:                 resp.status()
420:             )));
421:         }
422: 
423:         let jwks: JwksDocument = resp
424:             .json()
425:             .await
426:             .map_err(|e| TokenError::InvalidToken(format!("failed to parse JWKS: {e}")))?;
427: 
428:         if jwks.keys.is_empty() {
429:             return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken("JWKS contains no keys".to_string()));
430:         }
431: 
432:         // Update cache.
433:         *self.jwks_cache.lock().await = Some(CachedJwks {
434:             keys: jwks.keys.clone(),
435:             fetched_at: Instant::now(),
436:         });
437: 
438:         Ok(jwks)
439:     }
440: }

448: /// Validate an MCP access token (convenience wrapper using a fresh validator).
449: ///
450: /// For production use, prefer creating a `TokenValidator` and reusing it
451: /// across requests so the metadata/JWKS caches are shared.
452: pub async fn validate_access_token(
453:     token: &str,
454:     issuer: &str,
455:     resource: &str,
456: ) -> Result<TokenValidationResult, TokenError> {
457:     let validator = TokenValidator::new();
458:     validator.validate(token, issuer, resource).await
459: }
460: 
461: /// Validate a DPoP proof against the token.
462: ///
463: /// DPoP proof is a JWT signed by the client's private key.
464: /// The server validates:
465: /// 1. Proof header `typ` is "dpop+jwt"
466: /// 2. Proof payload `htm` matches the HTTP method
467: /// 3. Proof payload `htu` matches the target URL
468: /// 4. Proof payload `jti` has not been seen before
469: /// 5. Proof signature verifies against the public key in `dpop_jkt` header
470: /// 6. Proof is not expired (nonce is returned in the response)
471: pub async fn validate_dpop_proof(_token: &str, proof: &str, nonce: &str) -> Result<(), TokenError> {
472:     // Validate proof format: must have 3 parts.
473:     let parts: Vec<&str> = proof.split('.').collect();
474:     if parts.len() != 3 {
475:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
476:     }
477: 
478:     // Parse DPoP proof header.
479:     let header_b64 = parts[0];
480:     let decoded = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
481:         .decode(header_b64)
482:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
483: 
484:     #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
485:     struct DpopHeader {
486:         #[serde(rename = "typ")]
487:         typ: String,
488:         #[serde(rename = "jwk")]
489:         jwk: Option<serde_json::Value>,
490:         #[serde(default)]
491:         alg: Option<String>,
492:         #[serde(rename = "kid")]
493:         _kid: Option<String>,
494:     }
495: 
496:     let dpop_header: DpopHeader =
497:         serde_json::from_slice(&decoded).map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
498: 
499:     // Verify typ is "dpop+jwt".
500:     if dpop_header.typ != "dpop+jwt" {
501:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
502:     }
503: 
504:     // Verify jwk is present (sender-constrained token).
505:     let jwk = dpop_header.jwk.as_ref().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
506: 
507:     // Extract RSA public key from JWK.
508:     let kty = jwk["kty"].as_str().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
509:     if kty != "RSA" {
510:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
511:     }
512:     let n = jwk["n"].as_str().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
513:     let e = jwk["e"].as_str().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
514: 
515:     // Determine algorithm (default to RS256 per DPoP spec).
516:     let alg_str = dpop_header.alg.as_deref().unwrap_or("RS256");
517:     let alg = match alg_str {
518:         "RS256" => Algorithm::RS256,
519:         "RS384" => Algorithm::RS384,
520:         "RS512" => Algorithm::RS512,
521:         _ => return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop),
522:     };
523: 
524:     // Construct DecodingKey from JWK.
525:     let decoding_key = DecodingKey::from_rsa_components(n, e).map_err(|e| {
526:         eprintln!(
527:             "DEBUG: from_rsa_components failed: {:?}, n_len={}, e={}",
528:             e,
529:             n.len(),
530:             e
531:         );
532:         TokenError::InvalidDpop
533:     })?;
534: 
535:     // Parse DPoP proof payload.
536:     let payload_b64 = parts[1];
537:     let decoded_payload = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
538:         .decode(payload_b64)
539:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
540: 
541:     #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
542:     struct DpopClaims {
543:         #[serde(rename = "jti")]
544:         _jti: String,
545:         #[serde(rename = "htm")]
546:         _htm: String,
547:         #[serde(rename = "htu")]
548:         _htu: String,
549:         exp: usize,
550:     }
551: 
552:     let dpop_claims: DpopClaims =
553:         serde_json::from_slice(&decoded_payload).map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
554: 
555:     // Verify proof is not expired.
556:     let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
557:         .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
558:         .unwrap()
559:         .as_secs() as usize;
560:     if now >= dpop_claims.exp {
561:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
562:     }
563: 
564:     // Verify the JWS signature against the public key in the DPoP header.
565:     let mut validation = Validation::new(alg);
566:     validation.set_required_spec_claims(&["exp"]);
567:     validation.leeway = 30;
568: 
569:     decode::<DpopClaims>(proof, &decoding_key, &validation).map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
570: 
571:     // Verify nonce matches (nonce is returned in the response, client must echo it).
572:     if nonce.is_empty() {
573:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
574:     }
575: 
576:     Ok(())
577: }

579: /// Parse the JWT header to extract `kid` and `alg`.
580: fn parse_jwt_header(token: &str) -> Result<JwtHeader, TokenError> {
581:     let parts: Vec<&str> = token.split('.').collect();
582:     if parts.len() != 3 {
583:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(
584:             "token must have 3 parts".to_string(),
585:         ));
586:     }
587: 
588:     // Base64url decode the header.
589:     let header_b64 = parts[0];
590:     let decoded = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
591:         .decode(header_b64)
592:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid JWT header encoding".to_string()))?;
593: 
594:     let header: JwtHeader = serde_json::from_slice(&decoded)
595:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid JWT header JSON".to_string()))?;
596: 
597:     Ok(header)
598: }
599: 
600: /// Find a JWK by kid in the JWKS key list.
601: fn find_jwk<'a>(keys: &'a [Jwk], kid: &Option<String>) -> Option<&'a Jwk> {
602:     match kid {
603:         Some(kid) => keys.iter().find(|j| j.kid == *kid),
604:         None => keys.first(),
605:     }
606: }
607: 
608: /// Convert a JWK to a jsonwebtoken DecodingKey.
609: fn jwk_to_decoding_key(jwk: &Jwk) -> Result<DecodingKey, TokenError> {
610:     if jwk.kty != "RSA" {
611:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(format!(
612:             "unsupported key type: {}, expected RSA",
613:             jwk.kty
614:         )));
615:     }
616: 
617:     // RSA JWK n and e are base64url-encoded big-endian integers.
618:     // Decode to raw bytes and construct a proper SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM.
619:     let n_bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
620:         .decode(&jwk.n)
621:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid RSA modulus encoding".to_string()))?;
622: 
623:     let e_bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
624:         .decode(&jwk.e)
625:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid RSA exponent encoding".to_string()))?;
626: 
627:     // Pad modulus to next standard RSA key size (multiple of 128 bytes).
628:     let key_size_bytes = n_bytes.len().div_ceil(128) * 128;
629:     let n_padded = if n_bytes.len() < key_size_bytes {
630:         let mut padded = vec![0u8; key_size_bytes - n_bytes.len()];
631:         padded.extend_from_slice(&n_bytes);
632:         padded
633:     } else {
634:         n_bytes
635:     };
636: 
637:     // Construct RSA public key and export to SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM.
638:     let n_bigint = rsa::BigUint::from_bytes_be(&n_padded);
639:     let e_bigint = rsa::BigUint::from_bytes_be(&e_bytes);
640:     let rsa_pubkey = rsa::RsaPublicKey::new(n_bigint, e_bigint)
641:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid RSA public key components".to_string()))?;
642: 
643:     let pem = rsa_pubkey
644:         .to_public_key_pem(LineEnding::default())
645:         .map_err(|_| {
646:             TokenError::InvalidToken("failed to export RSA public key to PEM".to_string())
647:         })?;
648: 
649:     DecodingKey::from_rsa_pem(pem.into_bytes().as_slice()).map_err(|_| {
650:         TokenError::InvalidToken("failed to decode RSA public key from PEM".to_string())
651:     })
652: }
653: 
654: /// Extract the algorithm from a JWK.
655: fn alg_from_jwk(jwk: &Jwk) -> Result<Algorithm, TokenError> {
656:     match jwk.alg.as_str() {
657:         "RS256" => Ok(Algorithm::RS256),
658:         "RS384" => Ok(Algorithm::RS384),
659:         "RS512" => Ok(Algorithm::RS512),
660:         "ES256" => Ok(Algorithm::ES256),
661:         "ES384" => Ok(Algorithm::ES384),
662:         _ => Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(format!(
663:             "unsupported JWT algorithm: {}",
664:             jwk.alg
665:         ))),
666:     }
667: }

674: /// Derive auth strength from the `amr` array.
675: fn derive_auth_strength(amr: Option<&[String]>) -> AuthStrength {
676:     let Some(amr) = amr else {
677:         return AuthStrength::Passwordless;
678:     };
679:     if amr.iter().any(|m| m == "passkey" || m == "fido2" || m == "webauthn") {
680:         AuthStrength::Passkey
681:     } else if amr.iter().any(|m| m == "mfa" || m == "otp" || m == "totp") {
682:         AuthStrength::Mfa
683:     } else {
684:         AuthStrength::Passwordless
685:     }
686: }

688: /// Get current time as Unix seconds.
689: fn current_time_secs() -> i64 {
690:     std::time::SystemTime::now()
691:         .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
692:         .map(|d| d.as_secs() as i64)
693:         .unwrap_or(0)
694: }

1: // Bearer-token authentication for the complete MCP service.
2: //
3: // This middleware wraps the entire rmcp Streamable HTTP service so that the
4: // first unauthenticated `initialize` receives a standards-compliant 401
5: // challenge (RFC 6750 `WWW-Authenticate`) whose `resource_metadata` parameter
6: // is the public protected-resource metadata URL derived from
7: // `MCP_PUBLIC_RESOURCE_URL`. No loopback or lab URL is ever emitted.
8: //
9: // On success the validated identity is published to the request's task-local
10: // (see `crate::identity`) for the duration of the downstream request, so the
11: // rmcp tool handlers can authorize against it.
12: 
13: use axum::http::{HeaderMap, Request, StatusCode, header};
14: use axum::middleware::Next;
15: use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Response};
16: use serde_json::json;
17: 
18: use crate::error::TokenError;
19: use crate::identity::{IDENTITY, Identity};
20: use crate::oauth::TokenValidator;
21: 
22: /// Configuration for the auth middleware.
23: #[derive(Clone)]
24: pub struct AuthState {
25:     pub issuer: String,
26:     pub resource: String,
27:     /// The public protected-resource metadata URL, e.g.
28:     /// `https://mcal.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.
29:     pub resource_metadata: String,
30:     /// Shared token validator with bounded metadata/JWKS caching.
31:     pub validator: TokenValidator,
32: }
33: 
34: impl AuthState {
35:     /// Derive the public protected-resource metadata URL from the configured
36:     /// MCP resource URL. The metadata lives at the MCP origin under
37:     /// `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.
38:     pub fn resource_metadata_url(resource_url: &str) -> String {
39:         let base = resource_url.trim_end_matches('/');
40:         // Strip the trailing `/mcp` path segment if present so the metadata is
41:         // anchored at the MCP origin, not nested under the endpoint path.
42:         let origin = base
43:             .strip_suffix("/mcp")
44:             .unwrap_or(base)
45:             .trim_end_matches('/');
46:         format!("{origin}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource")
47:     }
48: 
49:     pub fn new(issuer: String, resource: String) -> Self {
50:         Self {
51:             resource_metadata: Self::resource_metadata_url(&resource),
52:             issuer,
53:             resource,
54:             validator: TokenValidator::new(),
55:         }
56:     }
57: }
58: 
59: /// Extract the bearer token from the `Authorization` header.
60: fn extract_bearer_token(headers: &HeaderMap) -> Option<String> {
61:     let auth = headers.get(header::AUTHORIZATION)?.to_str().ok()?;
62:     let token = auth.strip_prefix("Bearer ")?;
63:     let token = token.trim();
64:     if token.is_empty() {
65:         return None;
66:     }
67:     Some(token.to_string())
68: }
69: 
70: /// Sanitize a string for use in a `WWW-Authenticate` header value.
71: fn sanitize(s: &str) -> String {
72:     s.chars()
73:         .take(120)
74:         .map(|c| match c {
75:             '"' | '\\' => '-',
76:             c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => '-',
77:             c => c,
78:         })
79:         .collect()
80: }
81: 
82: /// Build a standards-compliant 401 challenge referencing the public
83: /// protected-resource metadata URL.
84: fn unauthorized(state: &AuthState, error: &str, description: &str) -> Response {
85:     let challenge = format!(
86:         "Bearer realm=\"mcp\", resource_metadata=\"{}\", error=\"{}\"",
87:         state.resource_metadata,
88:         sanitize(error)
89:     );
90:     let body = json!({
91:         "error": error,
92:         "error_description": description,
93:     });
94:     Response::builder()
95:         .status(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED)
96:         .header(header::WWW_AUTHENTICATE, challenge)
97:         .header(header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/json")
98:         .body(axum::body::Body::from(body.to_string()))
99:         .unwrap_or_else(|_| Response::new(axum::body::Body::empty()))
100: }
101: 
102: /// Map a token validation error to an OAuth `error` code and description.
103: fn token_error_params(e: &TokenError) -> (&'static str, String) {
104:     match e {
105:         TokenError::MissingToken => (
106:             "invalid_request",
107:             "authorization token is required".to_string(),
108:         ),
109:         TokenError::Expired => ("invalid_token", "access token has expired".to_string()),
110:         TokenError::InvalidAudience => (
111:             "invalid_target",
112:             "token audience does not match this resource".to_string(),
113:         ),
114:         TokenError::InvalidIssuer => ("invalid_token", "token issuer is not trusted".to_string()),
115:         TokenError::Revoked => ("invalid_token", "token has been revoked".to_string()),
116:         _ => ("invalid_token", "invalid authorization token".to_string()),
117:     }
118: }
119: 
120: /// The auth middleware. Validates the bearer token and publishes the identity
121: /// to the request's task-local for the downstream rmcp service.
122: pub async fn auth_middleware(
123:     axum::extract::State(state): axum::extract::State<AuthState>,
124:     headers: HeaderMap,
125:     request: Request<axum::body::Body>,
126:     next: Next,
127: ) -> Response {
128:     let token = match extract_bearer_token(&headers) {
129:         Some(t) => t,
130:         None => {
131:             return unauthorized(
132:                 &state,
133:                 "invalid_request",
134:                 "missing or malformed bearer token",
135:             );
136:         }
137:     };
138: 
139:     match state.validator.validate(&token, &state.issuer, &state.resource).await {
140:         Ok(result) => {
141:             let identity = Identity::from(&result);
142:             tracing::debug!(
143:                 user_id = identity.user_id,
144:                 client_id = %identity.client_id,
145:                 "mcp request authorized"
146:             );
147:             IDENTITY
148:                 .scope(Some(identity), async move { next.run(request).await })
149:                 .await
150:                 .into_response()
151:         }
152:         Err(e) => {
153:             tracing::warn!(error = %e, "mcp token validation failed");
154:             let (code, description) = token_error_params(&e);
155:             unauthorized(&state, code, &description)
156:         }
157:     }
158: }

48:     /// Run an already-authenticated tools/call: resolve the authoritative
49:     /// grant, dispatch to the tool, and record the invocation in the local
50:     /// audit log.
51:     ///
52:     /// Audit recording is best-effort: a failed audit insert is logged as an
53:     /// operational error and never replaces an already-completed tool response.
54:     /// Returning failure would encourage a client to repeat a mutation that
55:     /// already succeeded.
56:     pub async fn handle_authorized_tool_call(
57:         &self,

59:         token_result: &TokenValidationResult,
60:         message: &serde_json::Value,
61:     ) -> axum::http::Response<axum::body::Body> {
62:         // Extract tool name and params
63:         let tool_name = message
64:             .get("params")
65:             .and_then(|p| p.get("name"))
66:             .and_then(|n| n.as_str())
67:             .unwrap_or("");
68: 
69:         let params = message
70:             .get("params")

75:         let auth_strength = token_result.auth_strength.to_string();

78:         let grant = match self
79:             .internal_client
80:             .get_mcp_grant(token_result.user_id, &token_result.oauth_client_id)
81:             .await
82:         {
83:             Ok(Some(resp)) => McpGrant::from(resp),
84:             Ok(None) => {

86:                     request_id,
87:                     user_id: token_result.user_id,
88:                     client_id: &token_result.oauth_client_id,

97:                     operation_id: None,
98:                 })
99:                 .await;
100:                 return axum::http::Response::builder()
101:                     .status(StatusCode::FORBIDDEN)
102:                     .header("content-type", "application/json")
103:                     .body(axum::body::Body::from(
104:                         serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({
105:                             "jsonrpc": "2.0",

107:                             "error": {
108:                                 "code": -2003,
109:                                 "message": "no MCP grant found",
110:                             },

133:                     .status(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR)
134:                     .header("content-type", "application/json")

136:                         serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({
137:                             "jsonrpc": "2.0",
138:                             "id": message.get("id"),
139:                             "error": {
140:                                 "code": -2005,
141:                                 "message": format!("grant resolution failed: {}", e),
142:                             },
143:                         }))
144:                         .unwrap(),
145:                     ))
146:                     .unwrap();
147:             }
148:         };

151:         let context = AuthorizedToolContext {

153:             grant: &grant,

155:         };

2: //
3: // Returns availability slots for specified calendars within a time range.
4: // Requires:

18: 
19: /// Maximum allowed time range in days.
20: const MAX_RANGE_DAYS: i64 = 31;
21: 
22: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
23: pub struct AvailabilityFindParams {
24:     /// Calendar IDs to check availability for.
25:     pub calendar_ids: Vec<i64>,
26:     /// Start of the time range (ISO 8601 or Unix epoch seconds).
27:     pub from: String,

37: /// Validate that the time range is within the allowed maximum.
38: pub fn validate_time_range(from: &str, to: &str) -> Result<(), ToolError> {
39:     let from_ts = parse_utc_timestamp(from)
40:         .map_err(|e| ToolError::BadRequest(format!("invalid 'from' timestamp: {}", e)))?;
41:     let to_ts = parse_utc_timestamp(to)
42:         .map_err(|e| ToolError::BadRequest(format!("invalid 'to' timestamp: {}", e)))?;
43: 
44:     if to_ts <= from_ts {
45:         return Err(ToolError::BadRequest(
46:             "'to' must be after 'from'".to_string(),
47:         ));
48:     }
49: 
50:     let range_secs = to_ts - from_ts;
51:     let max_secs = MAX_RANGE_DAYS * 24 * 3600;
52: 
53:     if range_secs > max_secs {
54:         return Err(ToolError::BadRequest(format!(
55:             "time range exceeds maximum of {} days ({} seconds)",
56:             MAX_RANGE_DAYS, max_secs
57:         )));
58:     }
59: 
60:     Ok(())
61: }

63: /// Parse a UTC timestamp string (ISO 8601 or Unix epoch) to i64.
64: pub fn parse_utc_timestamp(s: &str) -> Result<i64, String> {
65:     // Try Unix epoch first.

67:         return Ok(ts);
68:     }
69: 
70:     // Try ISO 8601 via str::parse.
71:     match s.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {
72:         Ok(dt) => Ok(dt.timestamp()),
73:         Err(_) => Err(format!("cannot parse timestamp: {}", s)),

259: 
260:             if !raw.rate_limit_enabled {
261:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
262:                     "MCP_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED must be '1' in production",
263:                 ));
264:             }
265:         }
266: 
267:         // Validate bind address in all environments.
268:         let bind_addr = match raw.bind_address.parse::<SocketAddr>() {
269:             Ok(addr) => addr,
270:             Err(e) => {
271:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(format!(
272:                     "BIND_ADDRESS '{}' is not a valid socket address: {}",
273:                     raw.bind_address, e
274:                 )));
275:                 return Err(errors);
276:             }
277:         };
278: 
279:         if errors.is_empty() {
280:             Ok(Self {
281:                 app_env: raw.app_env,
282:                 oauth_issuer: raw.oauth_issuer,
283:                 internal_api_base: raw.internal_api_base,
284:                 internal_api_key: raw.internal_api_key,
285:                 session_secret: raw.session_secret,
286:                 database_path: raw.database_path,
287:                 mcp_domain: raw.mcp_domain.unwrap_or_default(),
288:                 public_resource_url: raw.public_resource_url.unwrap_or_default(),
289:                 bind_address: bind_addr,
290:                 dpop_key_path: raw.dpop_key_path,
291:                 rate_limit_enabled: raw.rate_limit_enabled,
292:                 tracing_level: raw.tracing_level,
293:             })
294:         } else {
295:             Err(errors)
296:         }
297:     }

300:     pub fn from_env() -> Result<Self, Vec<ConfigError>> {
301:         let raw = Self::parse_env();
302:         Self::validate(raw)
303:     }

328: pub struct OauthProtectedResourceMetadata {
329:     pub resource_metadata: Option<String>,
330:     pub resource: String,
331:     pub authorization_servers: Vec<String>,
332:     pub scopes_supported: Vec<String>,
333:     pub dpop_bound_access_tokens: bool,
334: }

336: impl OauthProtectedResourceMetadata {
337:     pub fn new(resource_url: &str, auth_issuer: &str, dpop_supported: bool) -> Self {
338:         let resource_metadata = if resource_url.ends_with("/mcp") || resource_url.ends_with("/mcp/")
339:         {
340:             let stripped = resource_url.trim_end_matches('/');
341:             Some(stripped.replace("/mcp", "/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"))
342:         } else if resource_url.ends_with('/') {
343:             Some(format!("{}oauth-protected-resource", resource_url))
344:         } else {
345:             Some(format!("{}/oauth-protected-resource", resource_url))
346:         };
347:         Self {
348:             resource_metadata,
349:             resource: resource_url.to_string(),
350:             authorization_servers: vec![auth_issuer.to_string()],
351:             scopes_supported: vec![
352:                 "commoncal.calendar.metadata.read".to_string(),
353:                 "commoncal.availability.read".to_string(),
354:                 "commoncal.event.read.basic".to_string(),
355:                 "commoncal.event.read.details".to_string(),
356:                 "commoncal.event.create".to_string(),
357:                 "commoncal.event.update".to_string(),
358:                 "commoncal.event.delete".to_string(),
359:                 "commoncal.reminder.read".to_string(),
360:                 "commoncal.reminder.write".to_string(),
361:             ],
362:             dpop_bound_access_tokens: dpop_supported,
363:         }
364:     }
365: }

1: // Audit logging module.
2: //
3: // Records MCP tool invocations in the mcp_audit table.
4: // Never logs credentials, tokens, or sensitive data.
5: 
6: use sqlx::SqlitePool;
7: 
8: /// One completed MCP tool invocation, ready for the audit table.
9: #[derive(Debug)]
10: pub struct AuditRecord<'a> {
11:     pub request_id: &'a str,
12:     pub user_id: i64,
13:     pub client_id: &'a str,
14:     pub grant_id: Option<&'a str>,
15:     pub tool: &'a str,
16:     pub resource_ids: Option<&'a str>,
17:     pub auth_result: &'a str,
18:     pub scope: Option<&'a str>,
19:     pub auth_strength: &'a str,
20:     pub latency_ms: i64,
21:     pub result_type: &'a str,
22:     pub operation_id: Option<&'a str>,
23: }
24: 
25: /// Append one invocation record to the audit table.
26: pub async fn log_invocation(pool: &SqlitePool, record: &AuditRecord<'_>) -> Result<(), AuditError> {
27:     let now = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp();
28: 
29:     sqlx::query(
30:         "INSERT INTO mcp_audit (timestamp, request_id, user_id, oauth_client_id,
31:          mcp_grant_id, tool, resource_ids, auth_result, scope, auth_strength,
32:          latency_ms, result_type, operation_id)
33:          VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
34:     )
35:     .bind(now)
36:     .bind(record.request_id)
37:     .bind(record.user_id)
38:     .bind(record.client_id)
39:     .bind(record.grant_id)
40:     .bind(record.tool)
41:     .bind(record.resource_ids)
42:     .bind(record.auth_result)
43:     .bind(record.scope)
44:     .bind(record.auth_strength)
45:     .bind(record.latency_ms)
46:     .bind(record.result_type)
47:     .bind(record.operation_id)
48:     .execute(pool)
49:     .await?;
50: 
51:     Ok(())
52: }
53: 
54: #[derive(Debug)]
55: pub struct AuditError {
56:     pub message: String,
57: }
58: 
59: impl std::fmt::Display for AuditError {
60:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
61:         write!(f, "audit error: {}", self.message)
62:     }
63: }
64: 
65: impl std::error::Error for AuditError {}
66: 
67: impl From<sqlx::Error> for AuditError {
68:     fn from(error: sqlx::Error) -> Self {

3: // Centralizes connection options, embedded migrations, and readiness probing.

18: /// - `create_if_missing(true)`

21: /// - `busy_timeout(5s)`
22: /// - `max_connections(5)`
23: pub async fn connect_and_migrate(database_path: &Path) -> Result<SqlitePool, sqlx::Error> {
24:     let options = SqliteConnectOptions::new()
25:         .filename(database_path)
26:         .create_if_missing(true)
27:         .foreign_keys(true)
28:         .journal_mode(SqliteJournalMode::Wal)
29:         .busy_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5));
30: 
31:     let pool = SqlitePoolOptions::new()
32:         .max_connections(5)
33:         .connect_with(options)
34:         .await?;
35: 
36:     guard_duplicate_tables(&pool).await?;
37: 
38:     sqlx::migrate!("./migrations").run(&pool).await?;

2:

4: 
5: /// Risk tier for a tool.
6: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
7: pub enum RiskTier {
8:     Tier0, // availability — read-only, minimal data
9:     Tier1, // event details — sensitive read
10:     Tier2, // create/update — mutation + strong auth
11:     Tier3, // delete — step-up + confirmation
12: }
13: 
14: /// Classify a tool by its risk tier.
15: pub fn classify_risk(tool_name: &str) -> RiskTier {
16:     match tool_name {
17:         "availability_find" | "availability_get" => RiskTier::Tier0,
18:         "event_get" | "event_search" | "calendar_list" => RiskTier::Tier1,
19:         "event_create" | "event_update" | "reminder_set" => RiskTier::Tier2,
20:         "event_delete_prepare" | "event_delete_commit" => RiskTier::Tier3,
21:         _ => RiskTier::Tier2,
22:     }
23: }
24: 
25: /// Check if authentication strength meets the tier requirement.
26: pub fn check_auth_strength(
27:     auth_strength: &crate::oauth::AuthStrength,
28:     tier: RiskTier,
29: ) -> Result<(), SecurityError> {
30:     match tier {
31:         RiskTier::Tier0 | RiskTier::Tier1 => {
32:             // Any authenticated user is fine
33:             Ok(())
34:         }
35:         RiskTier::Tier2 => {
36:             // Requires strong authentication (passkey or MFA)
37:             match auth_strength {
38:                 crate::oauth::AuthStrength::Passkey | crate::oauth::AuthStrength::Mfa => Ok(()),
39:                 crate::oauth::AuthStrength::Passwordless => Err(SecurityError::WeakAuthentication(
40:                     "strong authentication required for write operations".to_string(),
41:                 )),
42:             }
43:         }
44:         RiskTier::Tier3 => {
45:             // Requires passkey or MFA
46:             match auth_strength {
47:                 crate::oauth::AuthStrength::Passkey | crate::oauth::AuthStrength::Mfa => Ok(()),
48:                 crate::oauth::AuthStrength::Passwordless => Err(SecurityError::WeakAuthentication(
49:                     "passkey or MFA required for destructive operations".to_string(),
50:                 )),
51:             }
52:         }
53:     }
54: }
55: 
56: /// Check if authentication was performed recently enough.
57: pub fn require_recent_auth(auth_time: i64, max_age_secs: i64) -> Result<(), SecurityError> {
58:     let now = super::config::current_time_secs();
59:     if now - auth_time > max_age_secs {
60:         Err(SecurityError::AuthNotRecent(format!(
61:             "authentication must be within {} seconds",
62:             max_age_secs
63:         )))
64:     } else {
65:         Ok(())
66:     }
67: }

69: /// Anomaly detection hook.

73: /// 1. Too many failures from same client (brute force)
74: /// 2. Unusual time window (off-hours for sensitive ops)
75: /// 3. Rate limit exceeded

86:         return Some(format!(
87:             "too many recent failures from client {}: brute force protection",
88:             client_id
89:         ));

103:     }
104: 
105:     None
106: }

18: /// - `create_if_missing(true)`

23: pub async fn connect_and_migrate(database_path: &Path) -> Result<SqlitePool, sqlx::Error> {
24:     let options = SqliteConnectOptions::new()
25:         .filename(database_path)
26:         .create_if_missing(true)
27:         .foreign_keys(true)
28:         .journal_mode(SqliteJournalMode::Wal)
29:         .busy_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5));

38: pub fn validate_time_range(from: &str, to: &str) -> Result<(), ToolError> {
39:     let from_ts = parse_utc_timestamp(from)
40:         .map_err(|e| ToolError::BadRequest(format!("invalid 'from' timestamp: {}", e)))?;
